newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean securities body approves IPO applications.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean securities body approves IPO applications.

text.p: South Korea's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Monday it had approved 77.14 billion won worth of applications by SKC Ltd and two other companies to list their intial public offerings on the Seoul bourse.
A commission statement said subscription dates by SKC, Hankook Steel Co Ltd and Young Chang Silup Co Ltd were set at between June 19 and 20 with payment due on July 2.
SKC Ltd, a video and film manufacturer, plans to offer 4.8 million shares at 14,000 won each. The company is an affiliate of the nation's fifth largest Sunkyong Group.
Maximum individual share holding limit was set at 1,400.
Paid-in capital in SKC will be raised to 79 billion won from the current 55 billion.
Hankook Steel, a cast iron products maker, plans to offer three million shares at 20,000 won per share.
An individual investor will not be allowed to buy more than 900 Hankook shares. Its paid-in capital will be expanded to 4.8 billion won from 3.3 billion at present.
Hankook Steel shares were traded at 47,600 won last Saturday on over-the-counter KOSDAQ.
Young Chang, a producer of leather bags and other leather goods, plans to offer 342,608 shares at 11,500 won per share.

The commission statement said Young Chang's paid-in capital would rise to 5.65 billion won from 3.94 billion. Individual shareholdings of Young Chang cannot exceeded 1,000 shares. Its shares stood at 28,600 on KOSDAQ last Saturday.
The statement said the three companies were expected to obtain a Seoul bourse listing in mid-July.
